correctness.rationale: On the exact zero-sum Euclidean space and \(2\le a\le b\), the polar tight-edge criterion gives every facet normal; the Laplacian quadratic form of each is exactly 1. The balanced sign-orbit plus pure bipartition vertex weights are strictly positive, sum to one, have zero first moment and covariance \(\Sigma_J^{-1}/d\). This is an exact full-dimensional polar Löwner certificate and hence global John proof by polarity. The uniform signed edge measure has covariance \(\Sigma_J\) and each vertex has \(\Sigma_L^{-1}\)-squared norm 1 for \(\Sigma_L=d\Sigma_J\), giving global primal Löwner optimality; strict convexity/uniqueness and nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues complete the claim. Rational checker additionally verifies all moments/contacts for 18 parameter pairs, and separately exhausts polar potential labels in small cases; finite tests are not the general proof.

value.rationale: A complete all-parameter determination of two natural affine-normalized Euclidean invariants of a fundamental 2-parameter graph-polytope family is valuable: explicit parity-sensitive contact certificates, every facet and every vertex tangent, sharp universal symmetric John radius, exact eigenspectrum and volume. Complete-bipartite graphs with \(a,b\ge2\) include noncactus cases where the prior cactus decomposition does not apply; this is not merely a known facet count or individual example. The computation supports, but does not constitute, the claimed classification.
